topics.name: Behavioral & Your Story
topics.blurb: Intro, STAR stories, questions to ask, habits that cost offers

concepts.what: Answer to "Tell me about yourself": present role and years, two things you own today with one number each, one past role in a sentence, what you want next.
concepts.why: First question in every interview; it sets the frame for everything after.
concepts.ex:
"I'm a [role] with [N] years in [areas].
Today I own [thing 1, with a number] and [thing 2, with a number].
Before that I [one line].
I'm looking for a role where I can [what this job offers]."
concepts.tip: Rewrite the last sentence for each job posting. Practice until it's 55-65 seconds without notes.

concepts.what: Situation, Task, Action, Result. Prepare five stories of about 90 seconds. Say "I" for your part.
concepts.why: Most behavioral questions can be answered with one of five good stories.
concepts.ex:
1. Something you automated (with time saved)
2. A project you delivered end to end
3. A production incident you handled
4. A disagreement you resolved with data
5. Something you learned fast

Each: situation (1 line), task (1 line), actions (3-4 lines, "I"), result (a number)
concepts.tip: Numbers make stories believable: hours saved, machines, % fewer tickets, minutes of downtime.

concepts.t: When the honest answer is "only a little"
concepts.what: Say what you have done, what you have not, and how you would approach it.
concepts.why: Bluffing gets caught on the second follow-up; a clear honest answer scores well.
concepts.ex:
"I've worked alongside it: [specific thing].
I haven't owned it end to end, but here's how I'd approach it: [two sentences]."
concepts.tip: Interviewers hire people who know their limits and can reason past them.

concepts.what: Have three ready that show you are thinking about the actual job.
concepts.why: "Any questions for us?" always comes, and "no" is a weak ending.
concepts.ex:
What does on-call look like, and how often does it page?
How much is automated vs manual today?
What's the biggest technical problem you want solved this year?
How are changes approved?
concepts.tip: Leave salary and benefits questions until there is an offer.

concepts.what: Patterns that make strong people look weak.
concepts.why: Easy to fix once you hear them in a recording.
concepts.ex:
"We" for everything        -> "I" for your part
Tool lists with no context  -> what you did with one tool
No numbers                  -> add one per story
Blaming other teams         -> describe the fix, not the fault
Rambling past 2 minutes     -> stop and offer more detail
concepts.tip: Record one answer per day on your phone and listen back.

qa.a: Use your 60-second intro: current role and years, two things you own today with numbers, one line on earlier experience, and what you want next tied to this job.

qa.q: Why are you looking for a new role?
qa.a: Forward-looking and positive: what you want to do more of, and why this role offers it. Never criticize your current employer.
A real, job-relevant gap plus what you are actively doing about it (a lab, a course, a certification, a project). Avoid fake weaknesses like "I work too hard".

qa.q: Tell me about a time something went wrong.
qa.a: A real incident or failed change: what happened, how you restored service, the root cause, and what you changed so it doesn't repeat. Own your part.

qa.q: Tell me about a disagreement with another team.
qa.a: Show that you gathered data, shared it calmly, focused on the fix rather than blame, and kept the relationship good.

qa.q: Tell me about something you automated.
qa.a: What was manual and how often, what you built and how it runs, how you tested and rolled it out, and the result in hours saved or errors removed.
Map three of your strengths to three needs in their posting, each with a short example, and close with what you would do in the first months.

qa.q: What's the hardest technical problem you solved recently?
qa.a: Pick one where you did the diagnosis. Be ready for three levels of "why": evidence collected, what you ruled out, the real root cause, and what you changed to prevent it.
